speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you've had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings. Is the pain located specifically inside the ear canal, and does it happen when you touch the outer ear?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Otitis Externa with granulation tissue or retained surgical material causing post-tympanoplasty canal stenosis. The shooting pain upon eating suggests referred otalgia, and the difficulty wearing earrings indicates canal narrowing or irritation at the eardrum site.
